role: Heuristic detector of user corrections in recent user messages (asserted metric values, dashboard contradictions, explicit overrides) and renderer of the authoritative "User-stated values" system-prompt block.
state: knownMetrics / metricAliases / connectorRequiredMetrics / metricsLongestFirst / dashboardContradictionPhrases / correctionReplyOpeners / correctionReplyWords / explicitOverridePhrases (static lets, UserAssertedValuesParser.swift:97-294)
toplevel: Static phrase and metric tables; file name UserAssertedValuesParser.swift does not match the type it declares (UserCorrectionDetector).

units.does: True when any value was asserted or either correction flag is set.

Walks the given user messages newest-first, normalising spelled numbers, collecting metric=value assertions (first seen, i.e. newest, wins) and OR-ing dashboard-contradiction and explicit-override flags across all messages.

branches.cond: for each message, newest to oldest

flags.text: Flags are OR-ed over the whole window (caller passes user turns within the last 6 turns), so a single "you're wrong" keeps the dashboard training-load block suppressed for several following turns even after the user moves on.

units.does: For statement sentences only, tries each known metric longest-first, records the last value for each metric not already set and blanks matched text; then maps alias spellings (bsb/tsp/tbs→tsb etc.) when the canonical metric is unset.

branches.cond: metric not yet in assertedValues (an older message must not override a newer one)
for each alias whose canonical metric is unset

branches.effect: stores it under the canonical key.

flags.text: The bare metric "hr" matches the hours abbreviation: "slept 7 hr 30 min" or "ran 1 hr 20" yields hr=30/20, which renderAssertedBlock injects into the system prompt as an authoritative user-stated heart rate.

units.does: Removes sentences ending in "?" or full-width "？", returning the remaining sentences joined by spaces.

branches.cond: sentence does not end with a question mark

units.does: Regex "metric [connector] number" (number not a clock time); returns the value of the last match and the text with all matches blanked; connector mandatory when connectorRequired.

branches.cond: at least one match with a parsable number

flags.text: The number pattern rejects any digit followed by ":<digit>" (clock-time guard), so a pace stated as min:sec ("my pace was 5:30") is never captured although "pace" is a known metric.

units.does: True when the lowercased text (curly apostrophes normalised) contains a contradiction phrase or a sentence opens as a correction reply.
Scans sentences and stops at the first that isCorrectionReply.

branches.cond: sentence present and is a correction reply

units.does: True when a sentence starts with a "no/actually it's" opener and the next word is a correction word (not, different, wrong, higher...) or starts with a digit/sign.

branches.cond: opener matched and a following word exists
next word starts with digit, "-" or "+"

units.does: True when the lowercased text contains any explicit-override phrase (substring match).

flags.text: Plain substring matching on short phrases such as "don't call", "do not call" and "stop saying" fires on unrelated sentences ("don't call it a rest day"), setting explicitOverrideRequested which removes the dashboard training-load block from the prompt; "stop saying that" is redundant with "stop saying".

isExplicitOverride lowercases but does not fold the typographic apostrophe U+2019 the way isDashboardContradiction does, so iOS smart-punctuation input such as "don’t fetch", "don’t call" or "I don’t care what the dashboard says" never sets explicitOverrideRequested and the dashboard training-load block is not suppressed.

units.does: Renders "# User-stated values" block: a stale-data notice when contradiction/override is set and one "- key: value" line per asserted value; nil when no signal.

branches.effect: adds the "cached data is stale or wrong" notice.
adds the values header and lines.

flags.text: The type doc says the composer injects a "# User-asserted values (use these)" block, but the rendered heading is "# User-stated values (authoritative — fresher than any cache)" (docs/whitepapers/03-grounded-health-assistant.md:307 matches the code, the comment is stale).

units.does: Lines for prioritised keys (atl, ctl, tsb, acwr, hr, rmssd, recovery, sleep) first, then remaining keys alphabetically.

branches.cond: for each remaining key sorted, not yet emitted

units.does: Formats values: tsb signed one decimal, acwr two decimals, atl/ctl/rmssd/sdnn/hr/bpm/rhr one decimal, others %g.
